source: ZEBRA: Zero-shot Budgeted Resource Allocation for LLM Orchestration
summary: Zero-shot orchestration controller that divides a continuous monetary budget across dependent phases of a multi-agent pipeline without needing training data.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly relevant to per-run cost tracking, but HID-163 already covers token/cost telemetry. This would be a future reference once HID-163 ships.

source: INTENT: Online Planning for Budget-Constrained Tool Use (arXiv 2602.11541)
summary: Lightweight online planning framework for budget-constrained tool use; finds prompt-based cost feedback alone is insufficient to guarantee budget feasibility.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — confirms the gap tracked by HID-163; no new capability beyond what HID-163 intends.

summary: Studies whether LLM agents can predict their own token/cost/time budgets; trains small estimators as early-stop control signals, showing budget awareness can be decoupled from task performance.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — interesting signal for post-HID-163 work, but premature until telemetry baseline exists.

source: The Harness Effect: How Orchestration Design Sets Token Economics (arXiv 2607.06906)
summary: Empirical study showing orchestration layer design (holding models/tasks fixed) materially affects token cost across 22 enterprise tasks, comparing conventional agent loops vs sub-agent harnesses.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — supports eventual orchestration cost analysis but no actionable gap until HID-163 lands.

summary: Agent that evaluates itself on benchmarks, archives results, then edits its own codebase — a reflection loop where the agent both runs and improves itself.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — inspiration for run-outcome episodic memory, but HID-188 already tracks cross-run episodic memory injection. Distillation system already ships a simpler form of this.

source: Prime Agent by Prime Intellect (MIT, August 2026)
summary: Self-refining agent harness running on a persistent IPython kernel; revises its own outputs within the same reasoning session without a separate outer loop.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — interesting architecture but uses a persistent kernel model incompatible with AgentForge's CLI subprocess model. HID-188 covers the episodic memory angle.

summary: Lightweight agent template: Work → Complete → Reflect → Record loop that persists learnings to an AGENTS.md file after each task.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already ships a more sophisticated version via distillationAgent.ts and agentSkillRepository.ts.

source: LangGraph 1.0 GA with durable execution and agent middleware API
summary: LangGraph reached 1.0 GA with durable execution, a new agent middleware API, stable Python/JS surface, and Deep Agents higher-level layer with built-in planning and sub-agent management.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is its own orchestrator; LangGraph patterns are useful reference but not directly adoptable.

summary: Microsoft's official successor to AutoGen reached GA in April 2026; AutoGen moved to maintenance mode; community fork AG2 continues independently.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — architectural reference only; not adoptable into AgentForge's design.

source: Multica: TypeScript platform for managing coding agents as teammates
summary: Open-source TypeScript platform (~21.7k stars) for orchestrating coding agents as teammates with task assignment, progress tracking, and compounding skills.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — interesting parallel product but not a technique to adopt; AgentForge serves a distinct niche.

source: ODYSSE: Episode-wise Policy Optimization for Personalized Agentic Reasoning (arXiv 2607.25369)
summary: RL-based episode-wise policy optimization for personalizing agentic reasoning paths based on user interaction history.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — RL training loop is an explicit red-flag disqualifier per project evaluation criteria.
